cleanHomeApplied.explanation: The initialize response reported the requested clean home verbatim but in Windows extended-length form (\\?\ prefix). This is the canonical NT form of exactly the requested directory, not a different home. The server demonstrably used the clean home: it created its state files (state_5.sqlite, logs_2.sqlite, memories, skills, tmp, .personality_migration) inside it, and %USERPROFILE%\.codex was never inspected or referenced by the probe.

commandNotAttemptedReason: The harness enforced the mandated exact-string codexHome equality check; the \\?\-prefixed serialization failed that strict comparison, so per the probe rules the harness stopped before sending command/exec. No retry or second App Server was permitted.
classificationNote: CLEAN_HOME_NOT_APPLIED would be factually wrong: initialize did not report another Codex home, it reported the requested clean home in extended-length (\\?\) form, and the server materialized its state inside that clean home. Because the mandated strict string check nonetheless failed, the command was never attempted, so neither CLEAN_HOME_APP_SERVER_READY nor CLEAN_HOME_SAME_SETUP_FAILURE could be established. AMBIGUOUS is the only truthful classification.
limitations: The isolation question (existing home/config vs broken runtime) remains unanswered: no command/exec was sent in this run.

The strict-equality requirement did not anticipate Windows extended-length path serialization; a rerun comparing normalized paths (stripping the \\?\ prefix) would settle the question with one command attempt.
